analysis.title: Taiwan's GDP upgrade
key_insights: Taiwan Q3 GDP grew 14.36% y/y, up from 12.93% in Q2 and above ANZ's 13.0% forecast. Sequential growth was 3.21% q/q.
ANZ raised its 2026 Taiwan GDP growth forecast by 2.9ppt to 13.0%, assuming the semiconductor upcycle stays resilient through Q4. It expects 2.5% q/q growth in Q4.
ANZ raised its 2027 Taiwan GDP growth forecast by 1.5ppt to 6.6%.
Exports rose 21.12% y/y in Q3. Capital formation rose 26.36% y/y, the fastest pace since Q1 2010, which ANZ reads as continued optimism among technology manufacturers.

Household consumption rose 5.37% y/y in Q3 after 5.91% in Q2. DGBAS attributed this partly to an auto sales recovery and demand for new smartphone models, with retail sales up 7.60% and food-service sales up 3.93% y/y.

The main risk to Taiwan's cycle is its high exposure to the AI investment cycle. ANZ does not say the AI boom is ending, but notes concerns over the scale of hyperscaler investment. US technology stock performance may lead the semiconductor cycle.

Strong growth lets the central bank (CBC) focus on inflation. Governor Yang Chin-Long said this week that CPI rising toward 3% could prompt consideration of a rate hike, and ANZ says a December hike remains possible if Q4 CPI approaches 3%.
Authorities kept electricity and gasoline/diesel prices unchanged in October. Extending these quasi-fiscal measures could contain near-term inflation and delay any rate hike.

sector_views.rationale: ANZ's 2026 growth upgrade assumes the semiconductor upcycle stays resilient through Q4, and record-pace capital formation shows technology manufacturers remain optimistic.

tension_points.what_invalidates: ANZ's 2026 forecast assumes the semiconductor upcycle stays resilient through Q4. It says US technology stock performance may be a leading indicator of the semiconductor cycle.
